findings.issue: The custom-dimension rubric row says a configured custom dimension "is not required for severity coverage". The code does require it. step_normalize_review_dimensions (yaml 830-831) keeps custom names in config.reviewDimensions, and the registry seed (yaml 1027) writes "<custom>":false. convergence.cjs 1599-1614 then builds missingDimensions from config.reviewDimensions, so dimensionCoverageGate fails and the all_dimensions_clean candidate (cleanReviewStop, convergence.cjs 1127-1132) cannot form until the custom dimension is covered. Under expansive depth, reduce-state.cjs buildReviewFrontier (1997-2015) also marks a node answered only once every name in buildDimensionUniverse has evidence, and that universe includes the custom names. The reducer has no four-only coverage check that "severity coverage" could refer to: REQUIRED_DIMENSIONS is only the starting point of buildDimensionUniverse. So the doc presents custom dimensions as optional when they block the stop.

step_extend_completed_run on_fail says "Exit 2 is a usage error, such as a run that is not complete ... Any other failure halts with STATUS=FAIL". The command at line 588 ends the inline node script with `|| { rm -rf "$WORK_DIR"; exit 2; }`. That turns every failure of the script into exit 2 and so into the usage-error branch: an unparseable config, an unreadable state log, a JSON.parse throw. Only the gateway append (line 589) and the config mv (line 590) exit 1. A corrupt config or a missing state log is therefore reported as a usage error, not as STATUS=FAIL.
